subdomain: 2.5 Implement prompt reuse strategies (caching, modular prompts, Skills)

en.question: A moderation evaluation sends an identical rubric and demonstrations followed by a different test fragment on every request. Top-level automatic caching places its breakpoint after the fragment. Logs show repeated cache creation but no reads; requests are within cache lifetime. The unchanged rubric-and-demonstrations prefix alone meets the selected model/platform's minimum cacheable length, but no entry was written at that boundary. Which change targets the cause?

options.text: Keep the breakpoint on the changing fragment until automatic caching learns which earlier text is stable.
options.note: Automatic prefix checking looks for matching entries previously written at actual breakpoints. It does not learn and create an unwritten stable boundary behind a changing suffix.

options.text: Choose a longer cache lifetime without changing where the cache entry is written.
options.note: The existing entries include different fragments, so their cumulative prefix hashes differ. Longer retention does not make those prefixes match.

options.text: Mark only the changing fragment as cacheable and treat its block as independent of the preceding rubric.
options.note: A cache breakpoint covers the entire prefix through its block, not an isolated text fragment. It still includes the varying content.

options.text: Write an explicit breakpoint at the end of the unchanged rubric and demonstrations, with each test fragment after it.
options.note: This creates an entry at the reusable prefix boundary. Later requests can match that exact written prefix while processing their different fragments separately.
